title: Return Terms for Dispensed Insulin and Injection Supplies
content:
Dispensed medication on the Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program is never returnable, because state pharmacy rules forbid restocking a dispensed prescription. The three return terms each tier carries are therefore the same throughout:

| Tier | Return window (calendar days from the carrier delivery date) | Restocking fee | Opened items returnable for credit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Insulin Pharmacy Self-Pay Program | 0 | 0% | No |
| Insulin Pharmacy Commercial HMO Program | 0 | 0% | No |
| Insulin Pharmacy Commercial PPO Program | 0 | 0% | No |
| Insulin Pharmacy Medicare Advantage Prescription Drug Program | 0 | 0% | No |
| Insulin Pharmacy Medicare Part D Program | 0 | 0% | No |
| Insulin Pharmacy Medicare Part B Pump Insulin Program | 0 | 0% | No |
| Insulin Pharmacy Medicaid Program | 0 | 0% | No |

**Return window.** The window for requesting the return of unopened, sealed items, in calendar days counted from the carrier delivery date. A window of 0 means dispensed medication is never returnable.

**Restocking fee.** The fee withheld from the credit for an accepted return, as an integer percent of the amount the customer paid for the returned units.

**Opened items.** Whether opened medical supplies may be returned for credit.

## Questions these terms answer

*May unopened, sealed insulin pens delivered to the customer be sent back under these terms?* No. The return window is 0 on every tier, so dispensed medication is never returnable.

*What restocking fee would apply to an accepted return?* The figure is 0% on every tier.

*Are opened injection supplies returnable for credit?* No; opened items are not returnable on any tier.
